law: For example, you can subscribe to updates from a text field’s publisher, and use the text to perform URL requests.
You can then use another publisher to process the responses and use them to update your app.
The subscriber’s and associated types must match the and types declared by the publisher.
The subscriber uses the subscription to demand elements from the publisher and can use it to cancel publishing.
Every must adhere to this contract for downstream subscribers to function correctly.
Use operators to assemble a chain of republishers, optionally ending with a subscriber, that processes elements produced by upstream publishers.

Rather than implementing the protocol yourself, you can create your own publisher by using one of several types provided by the Combine framework: Use a concrete subclass of , such as , to publish values on-demand by calling its method.
Use a to publish whenever you update the subject’s underlying value.
You use to transform from one kind of element to another.
If your closure can throw an error, use Combine’s operator instead.
Use to accumulate all previously-published values into a single value, which you then combine with each newly-published value.
A subject is a publisher that you can use to ”inject” values into a stream, by calling its method.
Use it with properties of classes, not with non-class types like structures.
